questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The history of astronomy from Copernicus to today
How to become a TV presenter of science shows
A famous scientist's views on thinking scientifically
Why American schools are the best at teaching science
questions.why: They discuss Neil deGrasse Tyson, whose mission is to encourage scientific thinking among the American public.

questions.q: What is Neil deGrasse Tyson's day job?
options: He runs a planetarium in New York
He teaches science at a primary school
He works as a TV news reporter
He advises the US president on science
questions.why: Sam says he runs the Hayden Planetarium in New York's American Museum of Natural History.

questions.q: According to Rob, why have scientists come under pressure recently?
options: They have made too many mistakes in experiments
They are not paid enough by the government
Fewer young people want to study science
Critics with political views have attacked them
questions.why: Rob says Covid and the climate crisis put scientists under pressure from critics motivated by political views.

questions.q: What does Tyson say if nobody can repeat your experiment's results?
options: You should publish your idea anyway
Then it doesn't count as a result
Other scientists are probably jealous
You need a more powerful machine
questions.why: He says, 'if no-one can duplicate your results, it's not a result'.

questions.q: What does Tyson believe is the most important thing for a scientific approach?
options: Having a brilliant new idea
Remembering lots of scientific facts
Agreeing with other scientists
Knowing fact from opinion
questions.why: Rob says Neil believes the most important thing is to know the difference between fact and opinion.

questions.q: What does Tyson blame for many Americans being suspicious of science?
options: The way science is taught in schools
Scientists who appear too often on TV
The high cost of going to university
Newspapers that print too much science
questions.why: He says 'it has to do with how science is taught in schools'.

questions.q: According to Tyson, what is the most important part of science?
options: Memorising facts for exams
Doing experiments in a laboratory
Knowing how to question things
Reading books about the universe
questions.why: He says the most important part of science 'is knowing how to question things'.

questions.q: Why does Rob mention believing the Moon is made of cheese?
options: To tell a joke about his favourite food
To show belief alone doesn't make something true
To explain what Copernicus first believed
To show that some old ideas were actually right
questions.why: He says no matter how hard he believes it, 'believing it doesn't make it true'.
